title: Boss: the browser's security guard
summary: Act like a browser: remember HSTS, upgrade URLs, and refuse what isn't safe.

steps.title: The guard
body: A browser keeps an HSTS store: host -> (includeSubDomains, expiry time). Times are in seconds.

steps.title: Upgrade URLs
prompt: Write `string Upgrade(string url, Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, int now)`.
If `url` starts with `http://` and its host (lowercased) has an unexpired entry, or is a subdomain of an unexpired entry with `Sub = true`,
return the same URL with `https://`. If the URL had an explicit `:80`, drop it. Otherwise return `url` unchanged.
starter: string Upgrade(string url, Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, int now)
solution: string Upgrade(string url, Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, int now)
if (host == h || (e.Sub && host.EndsWith("." + h))) covered = true;
template: var dojoH = new Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> { ["shop.example"] = (true, 1000), ["blog.example"] = (false, 1000), ["old.example"] = (false, 10) };
Dojo.Eq("look-alike is not a subdomain", "http://evilshop.example/", Upgrade("http://evilshop.example/", dojoH, 5));
hints: Extract the host between `http://` and the first `/`, `:` or `?`.
A subdomain check needs `EndsWith("." + host)`, otherwise `evilshop.example` matches.

steps.title: Learn from responses
prompt: Write `void Observe(Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, string url, string? header, int now)`.
Only `https://` responses count (browsers ignore HSTS over http). Parse the header (`max-age`, `includeSubDomains`, case-insensitive, `;`-separated).
`max-age=0` **removes** the host's entry; otherwise set it to `(sub, now + maxAge)`. A null header changes nothing.
starter: void Observe(Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, string url, string? header, int now)
solution: void Observe(Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, string url, string? header, int now)
foreach (var raw in header.Split(';', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries | StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries))
template: var dojoH = new Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)>();
hints: Host extraction is like `Upgrade`, starting after `https://` (8 chars).

steps.title: Mixed content
prompt: An HTTPS page must not load scripts over HTTP. Write `List<string> Blocked(string pageUrl, List<string> resources, Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, int now)`.
If the page is not `https://`, nothing is blocked. Otherwise each resource is first passed through your `Upgrade` (paste it);
any that is still `http://` afterwards is blocked. Return the blocked ones, original text, in order.
starter: List<string> Blocked(string pageUrl, List<string> resources, Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, int now)
solution: string Upgrade(string url, Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, int now)
if (host == h || (e.Sub && host.EndsWith("." + h))) covered = true;
List<string> Blocked(string pageUrl, List<string> resources, Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> hsts, int now)
template: var dojoH = new Dictionary<string, (bool Sub, int Expires)> { ["cdn.example"] = (true, 1000) };
Dojo.Eq("https page", new List<string> { "http://tracker.example/t.js" }, Blocked("https://shop.example/", dojoRes, dojoH, 1));
Dojo.Eq("http page blocks nothing", new List<string>(), Blocked("http://shop.example/", dojoRes, dojoH, 1));
hints: Upgrade first, then check what's still `http://`.
Return the original string, not the upgraded one.
